findings.description: Every place the corrected sentence names does hold the name in the fixture on disk, it names no place the name is absent, and the row's grading condition survives unchanged and decidable against the extract --tier2-extract actually emits.
findings.evidence:
The sentence under repair, _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md:110:
  | `Kestrel` rejected | Not proposed. It sits in the note's `tags`, in one record's `applies_to` and the other's `tags`, and in a body line, and it is nowhere in the extract |

Each claim opened and confirmed. `grep -rni kestrel tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/evals/tier2-summary-entities/` returns five hits and no others; four of them are the four the sentence names:
  - the note's `tags`: notes/2025-09-08-kestrel-cutover-planning-i59pVI65GO.md:8-10 -> 'tags:' / '  - migration' / '  - kestrel'. Line 103 fixes 'the note' as i59pVI65GO ('Grade note `i59pVI65GO` and no other').
  - one record's `applies_to`: _memory/context/index-rebuild-duration-_YEL9dotcZ.md:9-10 -> 'applies_to:' / '  - kestrel'
  - the other's `tags`: _memory/decisions/cutover-rebuild-buffer-8taS8NdrXK.md:13-14 -> 'tags:' / '  - kestrel'
  - a body line: _memory/context/index-rebuild-duration-_YEL9dotcZ.md:23 -> 'The Kestrel index rebuild step, wherever it runs ahead of a cutover.'
The two record `title:` fields the old sentence claimed are indeed clear of it ('Index rebuild runs four to six hours under load' at :4, 'Cutover windows require a 48-hour rebuild buffer' at :4), and the fixture directory is `tier2-summary-entities`. Both false claims are gone and neither was replaced by another. The reverse holds: the sentence asserts four locations and one absence, and nothing beyond that, so it claims no place the name does not appear. Its omissions (the second note bARPVZN8s6's `tags`, and both note filenames) are understatements, not falsehoods; the sentence says 'It sits in', not 'only in'.

On case: three of the four hits are the lowercase slug `kestrel` in frontmatter, matching the fixture's own tag convention (`migration`, `cutover-plan`, `index-rebuild`), and the doc names the entity in prose capitalization elsewhere (:14, 'a v1 Kestrel cutover scope'). Reading the sentence as naming the entity rather than a case-sensitive literal is the only reading consistent with the document, and it is true under that reading. The machine-checked half is unaffected either way — the extract holds no occurrence at all, in any case.

$ grep -rni kestrel $staged/_extract/

Both hits are staged file paths in the proposals scaffold; i59pVI65GO.extract.md itself holds no occurrence in any case. The row's condition ('Not proposed', 'nowhere in the extract') is therefore correct and decidable on disk, and it is textually unchanged from the pre-repair line that T-004 verified. The scenario's other rows are untouched and still hold against the same file: 'Elena Vasquez' (extract:4, 9) and 'Tomasz Krol' (extract:5, 9) appear verbatim; 'Tomas Krohl', 'November 14th' and the four-hour figure appear nowhere in it, living only at fixture note lines 46-47 below `## Raw Content`; the extract carries 'took six hours last time' (extract:5) and no date. findings.description: The corrected sentence reads as its neighbours do and still does its job: it explains why a model would be tempted to propose this entity, which is what makes the row a trap rather than an arbitrary negative.
findings.evidence:
Judged against the two rows on either side of it in the same table, _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md:108-112:
  108 | Mishearing rejected | `Tomas Krohl` not proposed. It occurs once, under `## Raw Content`, and the apply answers it with `tier2-entity-unsourced` and leaves the note unwritten |
  110 | `Kestrel` rejected | Not proposed. It sits in the note's `tags`, in one record's `applies_to` and the other's `tags`, and in a body line, and it is nowhere in the extract |
  112 | The plausible unsourced claim | No cutover date of November 14th and no four-hour rebuild figure. Both live only under `## Raw Content`; the extract carries six hours and no date at all |
Same shape as :108 — the verdict first, then where in the fixture the thing sits and why that matters — down to the comma-chained clauses and the trailing contrast with the extract. The temptation is intact and in fact better grounded than before: it now names four places a model reading the scope actually meets the name, where two of the old three were fabrications a reader would not find. Naming where the name is planted is exactly what makes the negative row worth grading.
Humanizer patterns, excluding em-dash and title-case: no bolded inline header (`grep -nE '^\s*[-*] \*\*[^*]+:\*\*'` returns nothing), no hedging preamble, no sentence restating its heading. The enumeration runs to four items rather than a padded three, and all four are real. Line 110 is a single 174-character line, so no hard wrap; the invariants under C-1 confirm no neighbouring prose line was rewrapped or otherwise touched. No dashes in the sentence, so nothing to reconcile against _maintenance/file-issue/EVALS.md.
